MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MAY 16,2022
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Hill called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Kraig Hill, Vice Chair Dennis Robert Smith, and Commissioners Jeffrey
  Jennings, John Mazza, and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Richard Mol I ica, Planning Director; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant
  Planning Director; Trevor Rusin, Assistant City Attorney; Tyler Eaton, Senior Planner;
  Jessica Thompson, Senior Planner; Lauren Doyel, Coastal Engineer; Philip Coronel,
  Assistant Planner, Patricia Salazar, Senior Administrative Analyst, Johana Valencia,
  Planning Technician and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Wetton seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda, continuing Item No. 5A to a date uncertain.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on May 6, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Norm Haynie suggested those not present view the May 9th City Council meeting
  as an example of best practices for civil discourse. He stated his preference for a
  return to in person meetings without requiring masks.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of May 16, 2022
  Page 2 of 9

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION I STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Mazza welcomed the ability to directly engage applicants and staff
  in person. He asked Planning Director Mollica if progress toward repainting the
  wireless tower had been made.

  In response, Planning Director Mollica stated he had reached out to the Santa
  Monica College District again regarding the wireless tower. Their agency filed a
  Public Records Act request for the relevant Malibu Planning Commission records
  to review before they submit a response.

  Vice Chair Smith attended the Council meeting and enjoyed the dynamics of
  Councilmember exchanges with applicants and the public. He would like to return
  to in person meetings when safe to do so. He commended staff efforts and
  expressed hope that staff will be financially rewarded in the upcoming budget.
  The evening marked his 200th meeting with the City of Malibu.

  Chair Hill agreed there are benefits to live meetings but also from teleconferenced
  ones and would like a hybrid approach in the future.

  Chair Hill stated the tow yard plan required more consideration for the needs of
  eastern Malibu. He hoped data on tow yard use and vehicular violations would be
  collected and distributed for analysis. The Bell lot could be a viable location for a
  tow yard although action regarding the site was currently at California Coastal
  Commission since a portion may be designated wetlands.

  Planning Director Mollica stated the Bell lot is an active appeal with the
  California Coastal Commission, and he has contacted them quarterly requesting a
  date for the appeal to be heard. A public notice on the impound lot was scheduled
  to be distributed during the week.

  Vice Chair Smith noted that Councilmember Silverstein went to the California
  Coastal Commission about the wetlands on the Bell lot and his actions prevented
  cleanup of the site from taking place as previously scheduled.

  Commissioner Mazza clarified that Southern California Edison asked for a
  Temporary Use Permit to occupy the lot but relocated to Oxnard since they could
  not have immediate use. The lot is private property and not zoned for a parking or
  impound lot.

  Chair 1—lill noted that the Pepperdine Mountain Arena project on the north side of
  the campus with seating for 4,000 will impact Malibu, although it is outside of the
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of May 16, 2022
  Page 3 of 9

  City’s jurisdiction. Pepperdine’ s wastewater is self-contained but connected to
  Tapia if they exceed usage and he expressed concern about impacts downstream.

  Commissioner Mazza stated that Pepperdine refused to increase capacity for John
  Tyler Road.

  In response to Chair Hill and Commissioner Mazza, Planning Director Mollica
  stated Pepperdine prepared an Environmental Impact Report in 2011-2012. He
  wrote a letter detailing anticipated burdens to Malibu roads and wastewater
  systems at that time. However, the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors
  voted unanimously to approve the Environmental Impact Report.

  Planning Director Mollica also provided an update that the palm tree on Pacific
  Coast Highway near Latigo was removed. The Trancas Market was notified their
  events require a Temporary Use Permit. The unpermitted 6K run event was
  cancelled after contact by code enforcement. The Malibu High School has
  asserted that rototilling the campus near the baseball fields was authorized. The
  issue is under review.

  Commissioner Mazza asked if the report on weekend events could be published
  earlier in the week rather than on Fridays. Planning Director Mollica noted that
  Thursday afternoon is the norm, but two reports were released on Friday
  mornings due to technical issues.

  Senior Administrative Analyst Salazar explained that residents who want
  notification of all Temporary Use Permits issued may contact her or sign up for a
  newsletter on the City website. Temporary Use Permits require a notice. Special
  event permits do not have a public notice requirement. A special event permit can
  be submitted on a Friday that would take place the following day and private
  residences are limited to four per year.

  D.  Zoning Text Amendment No. 22-001 Amendments to the Malibu Municipal Code

  Recommended Action: Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 22-39

MOTION  Commissioner Jennings moved and Vice Chair Smith seconded a motion to adopt
  Planning Commission Resolution No. 22-39 as amended, adding a recommendation
  by the majority of the PC that I) paragraph three shall apply only to gas stations and
  the light trespass measurements shall be taken by the edge of the paved road closest
  to the property; 2) City Council and Planning Commission jointly receive an onsite
  visit with the City consultant to observe the impact of the proposed amendment prior
  to adoption of the ordinance 3) determining the amendments are exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act, and recommending that the City Council
  approve Zoning Text Amendment No. 22-001 amending Malibu Municipal Code
  Section 17.41 .050(G) of Chapter 17.41 (Malibu Dark Sky) regarding allowable light
  trespass from commercial and institutionally zoned properties onto the public right-
  of-way.

  The Commission discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT Commissioner Jennings requested a friendly amendment adding a
  recommendation by the majority of the Planning Commission that I) paragraph
  three shall apply only to gas stations; 2) the light trespass measurements referenced
  in paragraph three shall be taken by the edge of the paved road closest to the
  property; 3) City Council and Planning Commission jointly conduct field visits
  with the City’s lighting consultant to observe the impact of the proposed
  amendment prior to adoption of the ordinance.
